the emergence and maintenance of organizational trust is a function of the interaction among a variety of factors that are both personal and interpersonal in nature, as well as organizational and contextual.
the trust in organizations is a complex phenomenon that can be explained through a variety of factors.
trust is a multi-dimensional concept which has to be studied in the context of the organization and the relationships between individuals in it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the emergence of trust in an employee-supervisor relationship is the result of a complex interaction of individual, interpersonal, organizational and structural factors.

1) the employee's trust is a complex construct that includes several dimensions; 2) the emergence of trust is not only related to the characteristics of the employee, but also to the relationship between the employee and the immediate superior and to the organization's characteristics.
the emergence of trust is not a simple matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emergence of organizational trust is not a linear process.
there are multiple types of confidence that may influence the emergence of trust.
the concept of trust has evolved in a way that it is now possible to distinguish between different types of trust, each one of which may be more appropriate in different situations.
